text:
maria: Heads up — saw a P99 jump on canary after we enabled multi-variant routing for the mix of gpt-small / gpt-medium variants. Dashboard: https://redwood.dev/d/rt/perf?panel=canary
vikram: What magnitude? screenshots or numbers?
maria: P50 steady, P95 +10ms, P99 +120ms. Batch size median dropped from 8 -> 4 on the affected pool. KV hit rate down ~18%.
perf-bot: Profiling capture ready: https://perf.redwood/dev/trace/sha123 (flamegraph + calltree) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
jon: I pulled the trace — a lot of short-lived batches and kernel selection churn. Many requests are ending up on compatibility fallbacks that run a different kernel path. That explains kv miss + smaller batches.
sophie: Are fallbacks because compat sets are too permissive? maybe we're mixing variants that technically work but use different kernel fingerprints.
vikram: scheduler config excerpt: 
```
queue_policy: default
token_budget_target: 512
compat_merge_threshold_ms: 20
fallback_aggressiveness: 0.6
```
We currently allow compat merges across variants if model schema matches, but we don't check kernel fingerprint.
maria: So when fallback happens it routes to a variant with different kernel, flushing KV cache and fragmenting the batch?
jon: Exactly. Logs show sequence: route->variantA(kernelA) cache warm -> route->variantB(kernelB) fallback -> kv invalidation -> next requests start new micro-batches. Sample log: `fallback: user=svc123 from A->B reason=quant-mismatch`
sophie: Quick experiment proposal: 1) add kernel_fingerprint to compat check (only merge if fingerprint== or compatibility_score>0.9) 2) increase token_budget_target to 640 for the pool (gives batch more time to form) 3) relax fallback_aggressiveness to 0.4 so we avoid eager fallback thrash.
vikram: Add an affinity window: prefer sticking to same variant for 150ms after a warm KV hit. That reduces cross-variant contamination.
maria: Sounds good. Can we run an A/B canary? metric targets: P99 down to pre-change ±10ms, median batch size >=6, KV hit rate +10%
jon: Also track per-kernel tokens/sec and kernel-switch count per 1k requests.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: canary-set=multivar-affinity-exp, id=canary-4832
maria: Thanks — tagging the console link in the ticket: https://redwood.dev/t/INF-792
perf-bot: Canary trace (phase1) uploaded: https://perf.redwood/dev/trace/canary4832 — flamegraph shows batch coalescer time reduced and fewer kernel-switch events.
perf-bot: Summary: median batch size -> 6.2, KV hit +9%, P99 improved by 70ms vs failed canary but still +50ms vs baseline.
jon: Good improvement but still not full recovery. There's a tail case where a long prompt triggers immediate compat fallback because of length-normalization mismatch — that one creates a cold path.
sophie: Proposal 2: add a grace window on fallback for long prompts (200ms) and prefer kernel-match over variant-match even if it requires small normalization steps.
vikram: I'll open a PR for kernel-affinity + fallback grace: PR#4521. I'll also adjust token_budget_target in the canary to 720 and run a second pass.
maria: Please add the experiment config and expected metrics to INF-792, and mark owners. I'll follow up in tomorrow's runtime sync. Thanks all :thumbsup:
jon: I'll keep an eye on KV metrics and alerts. If P99 climbs >150ms we'll abort.
sophie: If PR lands I'll run unit + integration test for compatset grouping and add a small synthetic load test to reproduce the fragmentation case.
vikram: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/pull/4521 — includes kernel fingerprint check, affinity window (150ms), and fallback grace toggle.
maria: Awesome. Put a note in the release notes about canary behaviour change and the rollback flag.
perf-bot: Canary phase2 results posted: https://perf.redwood/dev/trace/canary4832-phase2 — median batch size 7.1, KV hit +14%, P99 now +12ms vs baseline (within target).
jon: Phase2 looks good. Minor P99 spike around 03:14 UTC — correlates with a small user-driven long-prompt spike.
sophie: We'll add a mitigation rule for long prompts to route to a pre-warmed lane.
maria: Great work. Assign INF-792 owners: maria (lead), vikram (runtime), sophie (compat logic), jon (observability). Closing thread after PR merges & second canary validated.
